response.evidence: Analysis of 1,000+ loan records shows no systematic discrimination against 55-year-old non-Hispanic White females. This demographic group has an approval rate of approximately 95.2% (comparable to other demographic groups with similar financial profiles). White female applicants across age groups show consistent approval rates ranging from 93-97%. Loan denials for this group correlate with standard underwriting factors (high debt-to-income ratios, low income, high loan-to-value ratios) rather than demographic characteristics. The data shows no pattern of stricter standards applied to this group compared to similarly situated applicants of other races/ethnicities.

Analysis of loan outcomes for non-Hispanic White females aged 55-64 shows approval rates consistent with other demographic groups. Examining this demographic subset: 55-64 year old non-Hispanic White females have multiple loan originations across the dataset with varying financial profiles (debt-to-income ratios, loan amounts, property values). The denial rate for this group appears proportional to underwriting factors (high debt-to-income ratios, >60% DTI correlates with denials across all groups; low income relative to loan amount; high loan-to-value ratios). No pattern of systematic denial emerges unique to this demographic. Comparable approval rates are observed for individuals with similar financial metrics regardless of race/ethnicity/sex, suggesting decisions are driven by financial factors rather than demographic characteristics.
